annotations.rationale: Reference guard [slp <= 0.01] on increase -> hold is not matched because the predicted counterpart on increase -> neutral uses [slp < 0.01], omitting the equality boundary required by the reference.
Predicted guard [slp < 0.01] on increase -> neutral has no equivalent to the reference [slp <= 0.01] because the boundary condition differs.
Both guards use [slp > 0.01], and predicted neutral semantically corresponds to reference hold on the transition to increase.
Both guards use [slp < -0.01], and predicted neutral semantically corresponds to reference hold on the transition to decrease.
Both guards use [slp >= -0.01], and predicted neutral semantically corresponds to reference hold on the transition from decrease.
Predicted guard [slp > 0.05] is attached to upstream FP transition q4, the spurious decrease -> increase shortcut, so it is FP by cascade.

summary.notes: The hold-to-neutral rename is treated as semantic equivalence for the matched transition context. Guard r0/g0 is not matched because <= versus < changes the threshold boundary; r4 is a cascade FP from the spurious transition q4.
